findings.claim: The duplicate-key guard in the field loop is inverted: `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey))` should be `!ContainsKey`. A string-keyed field whose key is new is now never added to stringMembers. For example, `[MessagePackObject] public class MyObject { [Key("myField")] public int MyFieldValue; }` gets a generated formatter that silently omits the field. It writes a 0-entry map and ignores the value on deserialize. This is silent data loss, and it also affects runs where SuppressSourceGeneration is unset (acceptance criterion 3).

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.StringKeyedFieldDroppedTests.StringKeyedFieldAppearsInGeneratedFormatter. It drives MessagePackGenerator over a type with one string-keyed field and asserts the generated source mentions MyFieldValue. Expected to pass on base and fail on head.

findings.claim: Because of the same inverted guard, `Add` in the field loop is only reached when the key already exists. A string-keyed field whose key duplicates an earlier string-keyed property (or field) therefore still throws ArgumentException. That is exactly the duplicate-key crash the other three hunks guard against, so the analyzer/generator still throws (AD0001/CS8785) for that input instead of reporting diagnostics.

receipt_plan.detail: Run VerifyCS.Test with TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck on `[MessagePackObject] public class C { [Key("a")] public int P { get; set; } [Key("a")] public int F; }` and observe AD0001/CS8785 from an ArgumentException in TypeCollector.
